textbookText: Unit 12: Universe
Section 'A'
Multiple choice questions.
Circle the correct alternative of the following questions.
1. Due to the effect of which force, are the celestial bodies in the universe situated at their position?
i) nuclear force of attraction ii) gravitational force
iii) magnetic force
iv) electromagnetic force
Ans:- ii) gravitational force
2. Which theory is considered the most realistic theory about the origin of the universe?
i) Hellocentric theory
ii) Geocentric theory
iii) Big Bang Theory
iv) Newton’s law of gravitation
Ans:- iii) Big Bang Theory
3. According to the Big Bang theory, how did the universe originate?
i) from the explosion of an atom
ii) from the collision of celestial bodies
iii) from the explosion of a star
iv) from the adjustment of nebulae
Ans:- i) from the explosion of an atom
4. According to Hubble's theory, which one of the following facts is correct?
i) The farther away the galaxies are the more the speed they will have.
ii) The farther away the galaxies are lesser the speed they will have.
iii) There is no relation between the speed and distance of galaxies.
iv) The gravitational force of the galaxies does not affect their speeds.
Ans:- i) The farther away the galaxies are the more the speed they will have.
5. Under what condition can an open universe be hypothesized?
i) When the average density is greater than the critical density
ii) When the average density is less than the critical density
iii) When average density and critical density are equal.
iv) When average density and critical density are not comparable.
Ans:- ii) When the average density is less than the critical density
6. What is the meaning of H in Hubble’s law: v=Hd?
i) height ii) constant of proportionality iii) gravitational constant iv) distance
Ans:- ii) constant of proportionality
7. What is the galaxy in which solar system is located?
i) Milky way galaxy
ii) Andromeda galaxy iii) irregular galaxy iv) Constellation
Ans:- i) Milky way galaxy
8. Under what condition can an flat universe be hypothesized?
i) When the average density greater than the critical density.
ii) When the average density less than the critical density.
iii) When average density and critical density are equal.
iv) When average density and critical density are not comparable.
Ans:- iii) When average density and critical density are equal.
Section "B"
Very short answer type questions.
1. How is galaxy formed?
Ans:- A galaxy is formed by the gravitational condensation of a huge number of stars, gas, and dust.
2. What is meant by the value of Hubble's constant is 73 km/s/Mpc?
Ans:- It means that for every megaparsec increase in distance, a galaxy moves away at a speed of 73 km/s.
3. What is centripetal force?
Ans:- Centripetal force is the force that acts towards the centre of a circular path and keeps a body in circular motion.
4. How does the big crunch occur about the future of universe?
Ans:- The Big Crunch occurs when gravitational attraction stops the expansion of the universe and causes it to collapse back.
5. What is the diameter of milky way galaxy?
Ans:- The diameter of the Milky Way galaxy is about 100,000 light-years.
6. What is astrophysics?
Ans:- Astrophysics is the branch of physics that studies the physical properties and behavior of celestial bodies.
7. What is meant by critical density?
Ans:- Critical density is the minimum average density of the universe required to make it flat.
